facts.statement: A label must match its prediction or observation through the intended unique identifier, rather than through incidental row order.
Check for repeated IDs before building an ID-to-label dictionary, because assigning an existing dictionary key replaces its earlier value.
Use set differences between observation IDs and label IDs to detect observations missing labels and labels with no observation.
Use keyed dictionary lookups to compare each label, observation timestamp and availability timestamp against the task-specific acceptance predicates.
Do not treat information unavailable at the relevant prediction boundary as an available input to that prediction.
Write assert predicate checks for the declared valid, boundary and failure cases; a false predicate raises AssertionError during ordinary non-optimized execution.

practice.objective: Implement one learner-defined Python audit function with learner-written imports for the supplied A/B fixtures and acceptance predicates. Check repeated observation and label IDs before accepting an observation-ID-to-label-and-timestamps dictionary. Use set differences to identify missing and orphaned labels, then keyed lookups to evaluate identity, label validity and task-specific timestamp predicates. Return one label-integrity verdict with affected IDs and author assert checks for valid, reordered, duplicate, missing, orphaned, misaligned, unavailable and declared boundary cases.
practice.success: The audit accepts valid records regardless of label row order, reports repeated IDs before dictionary replacement can hide them, distinguishes both unmatched-ID directions, and reports invalid, misaligned or time-unsuitable records using the supplied predicates. Assertions verify the verdict and affected IDs for every declared fixture, including the timestamp boundary.

live_code.required_skill: Write a bounded Python label-integrity audit using duplicate checks, sets, keyed dictionaries, supplied acceptance predicates and assert statements.
allowed_syntax: import statements for supplied dataset and timestamp handling
list, tuple, dictionary and set literals
string, numeric, Boolean and None literals
membership checks with in and not in
blocked_syntax: sklearn estimator fit() and predict() calls
live_code.starter_state_intent: Supply observation and label records using only observation ID, label, observation timestamp and availability timestamp, with illustrative IDs A and B. Include reversed label order and separate duplicate, missing, orphaned, invalid, misaligned, unavailable and boundary fixtures. Supply the task contract and acceptance predicates, but leave imports, the audit function and assertions for the learner to write.
live_code.observable_success: The returned verdict and affected IDs match each fixture's declared expectations. Reordering alone preserves acceptance; duplicate and unmatched IDs prevent mapping acceptance; keyed checks identify predicate failures. All learner-written assert predicates pass in ordinary non-optimized execution, while an intentionally false predicate raises AssertionError.
